correctness.rationale: A change to energy coordinates converts exact coordinate minimization into orthogonal rank-one projectors. The cost-normalized variables q_i=p_i/C satisfy c1q1+c2q2=1. An explicitly constructed unit vector w has squared correlations g c_i with the two regressors, giving the universal upper bound lambda_min≤g. The proposed positive q* meets its cost budget and has w as an eigenvector of eigenvalue g; its other eigenvalue is ≥g. Equality forces the same two independent linear equations and unique q*, even at rho=0. Exact-rational and numerical verification completed 35,662 supplementary assertions; finite experiments are not the proof. The sharp twofold bound follows from AM–GM and the stated joint limiting family.

originality.rationale: Exact comparison is made at the level of statements and objective functions. The cost-unweighted planar Kaczmarz theorem produces equal selection for two distinct directions; the new theorem minimizes a cost-divided worst-eigenvalue quotient and is nonuniform with unequal prices. Existing coordinate-descent probability rules optimize different volume-sampling or complexity-bound objectives. Full texts of the 2019 motivating paper, a 2018 expected-cost complexity paper, and two closest published mathematical records were inspected. No exact price–coherence identity or sharp factor-two boundary was found; historical E-optimal design overlap remains an explicitly disclosed precedence risk.
residual_risks: Classical two-parameter E-optimal-design theory, especially Elfving (1952) Section 4 with heterogeneous observation costs, may contain an equivalent or dominating formula; the accessible abstract could not resolve this.
Martinez and Wegman (2000) full E-optimal methods were not accessed; a specialized exact corollary might cover this model.
Unindexed optimal design or coordinate sampling literature may already contain an algebraically equivalent price–coherence rule. Publication priority is not independently validated.

value.rationale: There is a motivated algorithmic mismatch between curvature-only/upper-bound importance sampling and sharp one-step worst-direction progress under heterogeneously priced coordinate evaluations. The theorem solves all two-dimensional positive-definite Hessians and positive prices, provides a simple closed-form unique minimax rule, explicitly resolves the equal-price and orthogonal boundaries, and proves a sharp near-twofold improvement over uniform selection. The quantitative gain is a worst-case per-work guarantee, not a wall-clock claim; the result does not reduce to relabeling an established unpriced optimizer.
